events.event: IHSG closed down another 3.64% at 4,996.60, its lowest close in about 10 years, extending the MSCI-driven selloff after Friday's 11.57% crash; 656 stocks fell and only 100 rose.
events.key_numbers: Close 4,996.60 (-188.49 pts, -3.64%) from 5,185.10 · intraday range 4,907.37-5,012.86 (open 4,961.88, -4.31%) · value Rp25.15 T, 33.08 B shares · breadth 100 up / 656 down / 43 flat · market cap Rp8,863 T (from Rp10,627 T on 2 Oct) · week to date -15.83%, YTD about -40%
events.why_it_matters: The index fell below 5,000 for the first time in years, shrinking the value of ordinary investors' and pension-fund stocks.

events.event: Foreign investors kept selling Indonesian stocks, with over Rp1 trillion net sold in the first session alone, led by BBCA, BBRI and TLKM; Kontan counts 2026 foreign net sell at about Rp88 T and IHSG as the worst of 35 exchanges compared by BEI.
events.key_numbers: Session I 19 Oct net sell >Rp1 T · BBCA Rp670.8 B · BBRI Rp515.2 B · TLKM Rp205.5 B · AADI Rp44.4 B · 2026 foreign net sell about Rp88 T · IHSG YTD -40.04% as of 16 Oct, 35th of 35 exchanges (Kontan, partly paywalled)
events.why_it_matters: Foreign money leaving the biggest bank stocks is what drags down the rupiah and the whole index.

events.event: BEI and OJK met MSCI by video call on 19 Oct; BEI would not disclose the discussion and instead announced two reforms: labelling 1% shareholders as affiliated or unaffiliated, and excluding High Shareholding Concentration (HSC) stocks from the IHSG calculation.
events.key_numbers: Meeting 15:30 WIB, 19 Oct · HSC stocks stay tradable but no longer move IHSG (already out of IDX30, LQ45, IDX80) · count of HSC stocks not confirmed (a related headline says 80) · 4 earlier reforms already done · OJK says MSCI review is in November
events.why_it_matters: It shows how Indonesia is trying to answer MSCI's transparency complaints before any final decision.

events.event: BEI president director Jeffrey Hendrik argued Indonesia still meets all Emerging Market criteria and explained the ARB cut to 7% as a way to avoid trading halts and panic decisions, calling MSCI's Friday announcement unexpected.
events.key_numbers: FX reserves US$146.3 B · market cap US$498 B · inflation 3.28% · 9 stocks in MSCI Standard Index · ARB 15% to 7% for stocks above Rp10 (SK BEI Kep-00157/BEI/10-2026) · ARA unchanged
events.why_it_matters: Explains why shares could no longer drop more than 7% per day and what the exchange says about Indonesia's market status.

events.event: CUAN, BREN and DSSA each announced share buybacks after OJK's Rp2.1 T sanctions, and BCA announced a buyback window of 19-21 Oct, as listed companies try to support prices.
events.key_numbers: CUAN up to Rp500 B (19 Oct-31 Dec 2026) · BREN up to Rp1 T (19 Oct-31 Dec 2026) · DSSA up to Rp1 T (19 Oct 2026-18 Jan 2027) · BCA buyback 19-21 Oct under programme approved 12 Mar 2026 (valid to 11 Mar 2027), amount not stated · fines: DSSA Rp1.5 T, BREN Rp500 B, CUAN Rp100 B
events.why_it_matters: Companies buying back their own shares is a classic attempt to stop a slide, but it is small next to the foreign selling.

events.event: Brokerages estimate foreign outflows if MSCI downgrades Indonesia to Standalone, and BCA Sekuritas cut its end-2027 IHSG target from 7,100 to 5,200.
events.key_numbers: BCA Sekuritas base case about US$5.2 B (about Rp94 T), optimistic US$3.5 B · Mirae Asset about US$3 B from passive funds · JPMorgan US$4.8 B passive, UBS warns active investors could add up to US$15 B (CNBC Indonesia, 19 Oct) · BCA Sekuritas view cut from Constructive to Neutral · Reuters: about US$65 B market value wiped out on 16 Oct · these are projections, not realised flows
events.why_it_matters: Gives the first sourced size of what a Standalone downgrade could cost, answering the open question in our storyline.

events.event: BEI president director said share pledges are outside capital market transactions after Bank Mandiri disclosed it lent against shares of two Haji Isam affiliates, JARR and PGUN, in connection with the Jhonlin Baratama acquisition of Bayan Resources (BYAN).
events.key_numbers: Mandiri disclosure dated 18 Oct · loan amount not disclosed · pledges made by individuals, not the companies · Mandiri says credit is for capex, financing and coal-sector needs, not buying shares · BEI cannot cancel the BYAN deal
events.why_it_matters: Pledged shares are one of the ownership-transparency worries behind MSCI's concerns.

events.event: Rupiah closed at Rp18,046 per USD, slightly weaker, as markets expect further Fed tightening and wait for the Bank Indonesia decision.
events.key_numbers: Spot close Rp18,046 (-19 pts, -0.11%) from Rp18,027 · JISDOR Rp18,050 (from Rp18,052) · 15 Oct close Rp17,938 · next Fed meeting 27-28 Oct
events.why_it_matters: A rupiah above Rp18,000 makes imports, fuel and overseas tuition more expensive.

events.event: Bank Indonesia announces its October BI-Rate decision on 21 Oct (RDG 20-21 Oct); Kontan polls and analysts split between a hold at 5.75% and a 25 bp hike to 6.00%, with Citi calling a hike a possible pre-emptive step to stop equity outflows spreading to bonds and the rupiah.
events.key_numbers: Current BI-Rate 5.75% (held 22-23 Sep) · possible 6.00% · Deposit Facility 4.75% · Lending Facility 6.50% · 10-year SBN yield 7.169% on 16 Oct (reports of 7.46% after the MSCI news are unverified) · rupiah about Rp18,046
events.why_it_matters: A rate hike would raise loan and KPR costs but could steady the rupiah.

events.event: Finance Minister Suahasil Nazara said the 2026 deficit will be kept around 2.85% of GDP and that Q4 state spending will be about Rp1,300 T, higher than Rp1,200 T in Q4 2025, so year-end efficiency is not a spending freeze.
events.key_numbers: Deficit about 2.85% of GDP (July outlook to DPR) · Q4 spending Rp1,300 T vs Rp1,200 T in Q4 2025 · tax revenue Jan-Sep Rp1,607.6 T (+24.1%) · state revenue Jan-Sep Rp2,341.5 T · bansos through Sep Rp115.8 T · debt issuance through Sep Rp494.3 T
events.why_it_matters: It signals the government will keep spending to cushion the economy while markets are in turmoil.

events.event: Brent fell about 1.6% to roughly US$108 after the US waived some sanctions and tariffs on Russian exports tied to a diesel export deal, but Hormuz disruptions keep it near five-month highs.
events.key_numbers: Brent $108.14 (-$1.72, -1.6%) intraday 19 Oct · WTI $100.54 (-0.86%) · Brent had settled at its highest since 19 May on Friday · Kpler: Gulf crude flows about 8.5 M bpd last week vs over 20 M bpd the week before · US midterms 3 Nov flagged as risk
events.why_it_matters: Oil above US$100 keeps pressure on Indonesia's fuel subsidies and the rupiah.

events.event: Bahlil said coal has risen to US$154 per ton (calorie 633, benchmark not named) and the government will keep limited production relaxation; he also said Pertalite reserve is 16-18 days, expected to recover to 20 days within a week, as supply disruptions spread from Bali to parts of East Java.
events.key_numbers: Coal US$154/t (kalori 633) · Pertalite stock 16-18 days, target 20 days · RON 92/95/98 and diesel above 20 days · Pertalite Rp10,000 and Pertamax Rp15,950 unchanged · consumption shifted to Pertalite after non-subsidised prices rose from 11 Jun
events.why_it_matters: People in Bali and East Java are already queuing for fuel, and high coal prices tempt producers to export instead of supplying PLN.

events.event: China's Q3 GDP grew 4.5% y/y, beating forecasts, helped by a 36.3% jump in September exports.
events.key_numbers: GDP +4.5% y/y (Q2 4.3%) · +1.2% q/q · September exports +36.3% y/y
events.why_it_matters: China is Indonesia's top trade partner, so stronger growth supports coal, nickel and CPO demand.
